actions.action: Move plant to bright, indirect light or filter direct sun with a curtain
Rotate the pot periodically for even light
Check soil and water thoroughly when dry one inch down (weekly or two in summer, monthly in winter)
Check for overwatering signs (persistent moisture, weak stems, yellowing)
If pot is too large, transfer to a smaller pot
Inspect rhizomes and cut away brown, damaged portions
Replant in fresh potting media and water thoroughly
Take leaf cuttings as backup in case roots fail
Cut off brown stem sections to healthy tissue
Apply balanced houseplant fertilizer once or twice a year if nutrient deficiency suspected
Scout for pests (scale, mealybugs, spider mites)
Rinse stems under strong water stream to dislodge mealybugs
Dab remaining mealybugs with alcohol-soaked cotton swab
Apply insecticidal soap or horticultural oil for severe infestations
Remove scale-affected stems to healthy growth
Occasionally rinse leaves to remove dust
Repot into 1-2x larger container with fresh well-draining mix amended with perlite or bark

verdict.reason: A generic ZZ troubleshooting article that lists overwatering and root rot among many causes; the repot-and-water-less fix is present but buried, and its 'every week or two' schedule is tempered by a soil-dryness check, so it's not clearly harmful.
